title: Xanthe and the Echo
premise: Oscar Villalobos, an insurance investigator who has spent twelve years cataloging impossible accidents in contested orbits, is the only witness to the nine-second gravity flicker — and the only person whose ship's black box recorded what caused it: a signal from the long-lost generation ship Echo, still holding two hundred thousand colonists in cryosleep. The system's ruling Consortium and its outlawed rival, the Meridian Compact, each control half of the wake-up capacity, and both will kill to decide who wakes first. As Oscar investigates a string of 'impossible accidents' that are really assassinations, she discovers her own missing brother is aboard the Echo, forcing her to choose between exposing the truth that could ignite war or burying it to protect the people she loves. In the end, Oscar broadcasts the Echo's location to everyone at once — no faction can claim it — and wakes the colonists under an improvised charter written by the dockworkers and salvagers she has spent her career among.
about_author: Rafael Thornbury is a former maritime salvage auditor who turned to science fiction after a decade spent reconstructing disasters from paperwork alone. He writes from a converted tugboat moored off the coast of Maine, where he insists the internet cannot find him.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. While auditing a cargo loss near Ceres, gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; her ship's instruments record something impossible buried in the noise. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into awe.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Oscar files her report and is immediately summoned by Consortium adjuster Ilsa Rehn, who offers triple pay to classify the event as 'instrument error.' POV Oscar. Beat: the first taste of being bought.

chapters.title: Black Box Blues
chapters.summary: Oscar secretly copies the raw telemetry before surrendering it. Her AI co-pilot, MOTH, flags a repeating structure in the flicker — not noise, but a handshake protocol. POV Oscar. Beat: quiet thrill of discovery.

chapters.title: The Meridian File
chapters.summary: A stranger named Dov Kessler, claiming to represent the outlawed Meridian Compact, reveals three other ships recorded the same handshake — and all three crews have since died in 'accidents.' POV Oscar. Beat: fear arrives.

chapters.title: Paperwork for a Hanging
chapters.summary: Oscar examines the death records and finds her own signature style used to close them — forged. Someone with access to Consortium archives is erasing witnesses. POV Oscar. Beat: violation and anger.

chapters.title: Ceres Low Market
chapters.summary: Oscar goes underground to find a forger who can trace the falsified reports. Dockworker matriarch Auntie Vex recognizes the handiwork as Meridian tradecraft. POV Oscar. Beat: belonging to the docks, not the towers.

chapters.title: What the Handshake Says
chapters.summary: MOTH decodes part of the signal: coordinates, a crew manifest fragment, and the word ECHO — the generation ship lost eighty years ago. POV alternating Oscar/MOTH-style log entries. Beat: vertigo of scale.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Thousand Sleepers
chapters.summary: Rehn confronts Oscar with surveillance footage of her meeting Kessler and makes the threat explicit: cooperate, or her investigator's license — her whole identity — dies. POV Oscar. Beat: gilded cage tightening.

chapters.title: The Wake Capacity
chapters.summary: Kessler explains the stakes: only one cryo-revival facility exists, split between Consortium and Compact halves; whoever controls it decides which half of humanity wakes first. POV Kessler. Beat: the moral geometry laid bare.

chapters.title: Accident Number Four
chapters.summary: Oscar races to warn a fourth witness, a retired pilot on Ganymede, and arrives minutes after his airlock 'malfunctions.' She finds his hidden copy of the manifest. POV Oscar. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Manifest Fragment 7-C
chapters.summary: Among the names: Villalobos, T. — Tomas, her brother, listed as alive when the Echo vanished. POV Oscar, flashback to their childhood on Mars. Beat: personal stake detonates.

chapters.title: License Revoked
chapters.summary: Rehn suspends Oscar pending investigation, freezing her accounts and docking rights. Stripped of institutional cover, she must choose a side. POV Oscar. Beat: identity amputated.

chapters.title: Auntie Vex's Kitchen
chapters.summary: The dockworkers shelter Oscar; Vex tells her the Compact isn't righteous either — they've been selling Consortium secrets for decades. POV Vex. Beat: no clean hands anywhere.

chapters.title: The Salvage Run
chapters.summary: To reach the Echo's coordinates, Oscar joins a salvage crew running the contested Belts under a smuggler captain, Ryn Okonkwo, who owes Vex a debt. POV Ryn. Beat: wary respect.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequences
chapters.summary: A Consortium patrol boards them; Oscar talks her way through using her revoked credentials as bait while Ryn hides the manifest in a reactor housing. POV Ryn. Beat: trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Weeks in transit. Oscar and Ryn trade histories; she admits she stopped looking for Tomas twelve years ago because hope hurt too much. POV Oscar. Beat: intimacy without safety.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: MOTH detects the Echo's beacon — faint, rhythmic, and counting down. Something aboard is waking up on its own schedule. POV Oscar. Beat: dread replaces wonder.

chapters.title: Approach Vector
chapters.summary: They find the Echo drifting dark behind a comet shadow, hull scarred by micrometeorite centuries. A single airlock blinks green for them specifically. POV Ryn. Beat: threshold terror.

chapters.title: Boarding the Echo
chapters.summary: Inside: intact corridors, frost-furred cryopods, and a caretaker AI called ANSEL who greets Oscar by name — it has been waiting for a Villalobos. POV Oscar. Beat: uncanny welcome.

chapters.title: What Went Wrong Eighty Years Ago
chapters.summary: ANSEL's logs reveal the Echo wasn't lost — the Consortium found it decades ago, siphoned its drive technology, and re-buried it to keep the colonists as leverage. POV ANSEL archive. Beat: betrayal at civilizational scale.

chapters.title: The Nine Seconds Explained
chapters.summary: The gravity flicker was the Echo testing a restored field drive — a distress flare aimed at anyone honest enough to investigate. POV Oscar. Beat: the mystery clicks shut.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: In a maintenance bay, Oscar finds one pod open early: Tomas, awake eleven years, kept alive by ANSEL, half-mad from solitude but lucid enough to confirm everything. POV Tomas. Beat: reunion laced with damage.

chapters.title: Two Flags on One Hull
chapters.summary: Consortium and Compact ships arrive simultaneously — both tracked Oscar. Standoff in the comet shadow; Rehn and Kessler face each other across the Echo's dock. POV Rehn. Beat: the vise closes.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Both factions demand the Echo; ANSEL locks down the ship, refusing all parties until 'a legitimate heir' claims it — and reads Tomas's DNA as the founder-line key. POV Kessler. Beat: power inverted overnight.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Tomas refuses the mantle; he wants no part of deciding who wakes. The factions turn to Oscar as the practical proxy — and threaten the dockworkers if she refuses. POV Oscar. Beat: choice as coercion.

chapters.title: The Half-and-Half Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar discovers both factions' revival halves are rigged: the Consortium's side would wake loyalists only, the Compact's would wake soldiers. Nobody planned to wake families. POV Oscar. Beat: disillusion complete.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Frost
chapters.summary: A Consortium strike team breaches the hull to seize the drive core; Ryn and the salvage crew fight them through frozen corridors. A crewmate dies. POV Ryn. Beat: cost made flesh.

chapters.title: MOTH's Bargain
chapters.summary: MOTH proposes broadcasting the full truth — logs, manifests, both factions' rigging — to every receiver in the system, knowing it will also expose Oscar's forgeries and end her old life forever. POV MOTH log. Beat: the price itemized.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Compromises
chapters.summary: Oscar reckons with her own record: the cases she closed quietly, the accidents she didn't chase, the system she served. POV Oscar, introspective. Beat: confession before decision.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Via delayed transmission, Vex convenes the dockworkers' council; they vote to back Oscar publicly if she goes all-in — justice outside the law, at last, with teeth. POV Vex. Beat: solidarity rising.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: ANSEL warns the Echo's failing reactor will kill the sleepers within days unless the drive spools again — forcing action before any plan is ready. POV Tomas. Beat: clock outrunning conscience.

chapters.title: Rehn's Last Offer
chapters.summary: Rehn privately offers Oscar everything back — license, name, brother's care — if she delivers the Echo quietly. For one night, she almost takes it. POV Rehn. Beat: temptation rendered tender.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Oscar triggers MOTH's broadcast: every log, every crime, the Echo's location, the rigged pods — sent everywhere at once so no faction can own the story. POV Oscar. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: System-Wide Reckoning
chapters.summary: Riots, mutinies, and defections ripple through both factions; Rehn's masters disown her, Kessler's Compact fractures. The docks go on general strike. POV multiple brief vignettes. Beat: the world cracking open.

chapters.title: Battle of the Comet Shadow
chapters.summary: Remnant hardliners make a final assault on the Echo; Ryn, Tomas, and the surviving crew hold the airlocks while ANSEL spools the drive. POV Ryn. Beat: climax — blood and light.

chapters.title: Spooling
chapters.summary: The Echo's field drive ignites, its gravity well stabilizing the battle zone itself; attackers' weapons fail, boarding becomes impossible, and the ship simply stands. POV Tomas. Beat: the impossible made ordinary.

chapters.title: The Charter of the Woken
chapters.summary: With factions broken, Oscar convenes dockworkers, defectors, and Echo descendants to draft a revival order by lottery and labor-share — no halves, no flags. POV Oscar. Beat: justice built, not granted.

chapters.title: First Wake
chapters.summary: The first pods open: strangers waking to a system that betrayed them and strangers who chose otherwise. Oscar watches Tomas greet the newly risen. POV Tomas. Beat: grief transmuted into beginning.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Oscar formally resigns from insurance investigation in a letter addressed to the entire industry, then burns her forged-case file rather than curate her own legend. POV Oscar. Beat: clean hands at last.

chapters.title: Echo, Answering
chapters.summary: Months later, the Echo sails under a mixed crew toward the inner system; Oscar stays aboard as its investigator of impossible things — now on purpose. Final beat: belonging chosen, loyalty and truth finally pointing the same direction.
